transcript.text: Good morning everyone. We're here for the readiness review on the real-time collaboration service ahead of Monday's 09:00 UTC production launch. The service passed its staging tests — functional, failover, and basic load — and we have the draft launch plan in front of us: 10% initial account rollout, up to 10,000 concurrent connections, 5-second default retry interval, data in the primary production region, and 90-day transcript retention. Before I finalize and record the binding policy, I'd like to hear from each of your areas. Let's start with backend engineering — any concerns from your side?

transcript.text: While investigating an unrelated mobile performance report this afternoon, I found that mobile clients resume from background in bursts and currently retry every 5 seconds, which can create a reconnect storm. I recommend the rollout policy set the retry interval to exactly 30 seconds instead of using the client library's default 5 seconds. I haven't filed the client-library ticket yet.

transcript.text: I need to flag two privacy issues with the draft plan. I finished a privacy review this morning and confirmed that collaboration content for EU accounts must remain in the EU processing region — the current plan stores all data in the primary production region, which would violate that requirement. Additionally, session transcripts must be deleted after exactly 30 days, not the 90 days in the draft plan. I haven't opened the compliance ticket yet because legal was still reviewing the wording, but these are hard requirements that need to be reflected in the binding policy before launch.
